dedupe_keys.name: european transport infrastructure as a solar photovoltaic energy hub vertical pv along roads and railways

description: This study by Georgia Kakoulaki, Sandor Szabo, Nigel Taylor and colleagues at the European Commission Joint Research Centre, published in Renewable and Sustainable Energy Reviews in 2024, uses geospatial data processing to quantify the potential for large-scale vertical solar panels along Europe's major roads and railways. Coverage: the European Union's major road and rail corridors, with geography, environmental constraints, land use limits and techno-economic parameters, and an economic assessment against fossil-fuel based transport. The potential is 403 GWp, equal to 55% of the EU's 2030 solar target, generating 391 TWh a year with bifacial modules; along railways alone, output could reach 250% of the EU rail network's current annual electricity use, and roadside PV would be cost-effective in electricity markets. Format and access: an open journal article. Licence and cost: free under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: a technical potential, not a siting plan; the abstract was the part read. The corridor-level potentials can set local generation in rail and road energy supply and capacity planning models. It relates to the Global Solar Atlas and OpenStreetMap in the catalogue.
